exposure: Transcatheter arterial embolization (TAE) with gelatin sponge (GS) particles
Transcatheter arterial embolization (TAE) with polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) particles
outcome: Time for serum b-hCG level to return to normal
Time for the return of menstrual cycle
cohort: The participants were 35 patients diagnosed with cesarean scar pregnancy (CSP), divided into a GS group (n=22) and a PVA group (n=13).
finding: TAE with either GS or PVA particles was effective for CSP treatment, though patients in the PVA group were older, had more abortions/curettages, longer times since last cesarean, and experienced a shorter time for menstrual cycle return but a higher incidence of abnormal menstrual blood volume reduction compared to the GS group.
followup_time: The abstract mentions a 'follow-up period' without specifying an exact duration.
